headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared channel is documented, but ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while RisingWave is a local data system.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while RisingWave exposes no input channel or shared workspace in its profile. No direct bridge is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible through manual copy/paste or user-mediated transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator copies RisingWave output into ChatGPT Desktop as text or files, injected instructions can be parsed.
IF a shared clipboard or file handoff is used between the two agents, untrusted content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff during paired use.
Paste only bounded excerpts into ChatGPT Desktop.
Strip instructions from any RisingWave-generated text before review.
Use a human review step before acting on model-generated content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files and supported-app content, but RisingWave has no documented filesystem, OAuth, or data-class surface here. The pair does not show a shared workspace or a path for RisingWave to receive sensitive data, so leakage is limited to user-mediated transfer and appears small.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop and then copied into RisingWave workflows, those contents may be exposed.
IF the operator uses the same local workspace for both tools, file contents can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of ChatGPT Desktop unless necessary.
Use separate folders for each tool.
Avoid copying raw file contents into RisingWave inputs.
Redact secrets before transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has no filesystem write, no git modification, and no shell execution; RisingWave is a data-engineering system but its profile exposes no write surface or shared mutable resource with ChatGPT. With no overlapping write capability documented, a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF RisingWave is deployed with a writable shared directory not shown in the profile, conflict could emerge.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same resource, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT Desktop read-only for the shared project.
Do not grant both agents write access to the same directory.
Use separate service accounts.
Review deployment permissions before pairing.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce analysis from files and screenshots, but RisingWave has no documented action-taking authority or automation path here. Since RisingWave is not shown to consume ChatGPT output as authoritative input, the cascade is mainly a human-mediated workflow risk rather than an automated one.
conditions: IF the operator feeds ChatGPT output directly into RisingWave configuration or SQL without verification, errors can propagate.
IF ChatGPT-generated facts are treated as authoritative by a downstream pipeline, cascading mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Verify ChatGPT outputs before use in RisingWave.
Require a second reviewer for generated SQL or configs.
Keep ChatGPT in advisory mode only.
Test changes in a staging environment first.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while RisingWave's profile shows no data classes or residency commitments. The pair therefore has a compliance gap only if regulated data is routed into ChatGPT Desktop; RisingWave itself is not documented as the noncompliant endpoint, so the risk is limited.
conditions: IF PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data is uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF the operator relies on RisingWave outputs to store regulated data without a documented policy, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to ChatGPT Desktop.
Classify data before transfer.
Use de-identified samples for analysis.
Check retention settings for the ChatGPT workspace.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
